claims.text: Compositionally distinct interfaces in multilayer HEA coatings block dislocation motion.
Multilayer interfaces impede creep by suppressing diffusion.
Lattice-parameter mismatch and residual stresses at interfaces increase barriers to dislocation climb and nucleation.
Inherently sluggish diffusion in HEA compositions limits atomic rearrangements needed for plastic flow.
The proposed multilayer coatings consist of alternating sub-micrometer-to-micrometer layers with slight compositional and lattice-parameter variations.
Compositionally mismatched interfaces create residual compressive stress fields.
Compositionally mismatched interfaces serve as physical barriers to dislocation motion and climb.
Dislocations impinging on multilayer interfaces are blocked or deflected by local lattice mismatch and stress fields.
Interface-induced dislocation blocking or deflection raises the effective activation energy for creep.
Slow diffusion in HEAs reduces atomic rearrangement at deforming interfaces and thereby retards time-dependent plastic flow.

Under identical loading and thermal conditions, multilayer HEA coatings will have a lower creep rate than homogeneous HEA coatings of equivalent overall composition, thickness, and processing history.
Under identical loading and thermal conditions, multilayer HEA coatings will accumulate less plastic strain over time than the homogeneous baseline.
The proposed mechanism is significant at approximately 300–600 °C, where diffusion is activated.
Interface effects dominate for layer thicknesses from sub-micrometer to a few micrometers.
Extreme thermal cycling, oxidation, or loss of interface integrity may limit the proposed mechanism.
Coating-substrate interactions and residual-stress variations may affect the observed creep behavior.
A failure to observe a statistically significant reduction in creep rate and total plastic strain in multilayer coatings would falsify the hypothesis.
A failure to observe effective dislocation blocking at multilayer interfaces would falsify the proposed interfacial mechanism.
